title: Introduce Store struct and expand go_http_server handlers
description: Brownfield Go migration: add persistent in-memory storage via a Store struct and expose CreateItem and DeleteItem handlers alongside the existing ListItems.

task_spec.prompt:
Migrate internal/handler/items.go to use a Store struct. All existing tests must still pass.

Add to internal/handler/items.go:

  type Item struct {
    ID    int     `json:"id"`
    Name  string  `json:"name"`
    Value float64 `json:"value"`
  }

  type Store struct { /* mu sync.Mutex; items []Item; nextID int */ }

  func NewStore() *Store
    — initialises empty store with nextID=1

  func (s *Store) Add(name string, value float64) Item
    — assigns next ID, appends to store, returns the new Item

  func (s *Store) All() []Item
    — returns a copy of all items (or empty slice)

  func (s *Store) Delete(id int) bool
    — removes the item with the given ID; returns true if found, false otherwise

  var defaultStore = NewStore()

  func CreateItem(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)
    — POST only (405 otherwise); reads JSON body with 'name' (string) and 'value' (float64)
    — calls defaultStore.Add; writes the new item as JSON with status 201

  func DeleteItem(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)
    — DELETE only (405 otherwise); reads query param 'id' as int (400 if missing/invalid)
    — calls defaultStore.Delete; 204 on success, 404 if not found

Update ListItems to call defaultStore.All() instead of returning a hard-coded empty slice.

Add at least 4 tests for the Store struct methods.
The existing TestListItems test must still pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: Item struct with ID, Name, Value fields
Store.Delete removes by ID, returns bool
CreateItem POST handler writes 201 with new item JSON
ListItems now returns items from store
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `go test ./...` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
